top.title: 6,000 Flight Cancelled: US air travel resumption will ‘take time’
top.description: Flights in the United States were resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time. The nationwide stop on Friday sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events. The incident marked only the second time such an alert had been issued in US airspace — which is among the busiest in the world — since the 9/11 attacks. The ground stop lasted around four hours and was lifted at 8:15 pm Eastern Time (0115 GMT Saturday). Federal Aviation Administration officials reopened the airspace on Friday night “after restoring full functionality” at air traffic control facilities, according to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy. “It will take us time (to) resume normal operations… Our top priority is the safety of you and your family when you fly,” Duffy said. Administration officials blamed the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment, adding there was no evidence of foul play. “This is a legacy system problem,” Duffy said. “We have old, old switches, old routers. “We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded.” Duffy had formally asked Congress on Thursday for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control System. As the ground stop was lifted, he repeated his plea. “I’m going to say it a million times: the Congress has to give the resources to the president so he can finish this bill,” he said. 6,000 flights canceled There were almost 6,000 flights canceled, including some international routes, according to FlightAware, a tracking platform. Footage from airports around the country showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways. Passengers thronged concourses, desperate for information about an outage that had thrown their plans into chaos. “We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too,” said Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California. A nationwide ground stop is highly unusual. There was one such stop in January 2023 when a pilot notification system failed, but the only other national stop happened in the wake of the 9/11 attacks in September 2001, when no aircraft took to the skies for days. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stressed there was no evidence of any hostile action on Friday. “We’ve seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack or (AI) attack,” he told a news conference. He also ruled out any connection with the outage that affected Microsoft this week, knocking email systems offline for millions of users, public services and businesses worldwide. top.title: The challenge that brought Nunes out of retirement
top.description: Amanda Nunes is one of four simultaneous two-division champions in UFC history [Getty Images] It was always going to take a special challenge to bring Amanda Nunes out of retirement. The Brazilian left the UFC in 2023 as the most successful women's mixed martial artist of all time, and with a strong claim to be the greatest ever, regardless of gender. A former featherweight and bantamweight champion, Nunes is the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts. During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko. After Nunes was eventually dethroned by Julianna Pena in one of the biggest upsets of all time, she then regained her title in emphatic fashion. Nunes was so dominant, she ran out of challengers and left the sport feeling like she had completed MMA. That was until Kayla Harrison came along. "When Kayla signed with the UFC and I saw the division with some new girls it excited me," said Nunes. "Because I cleaned both divisions and didn't have anything to do any more. That was when I was sure I wanted to do this again." American Harrison is a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo who became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion after transitioning to MMA. After joining the UFC in 2024, Harrison won the bantamweight title in only her third fight with the promotion. The contest between 36-year-old Harrison and 38-year-old Nunes is being described by pundits as one of the biggest women's fights in UFC history. The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, before Nunes left in 2022. They were originally set to fight in January, but the fight got postponed after Harrison required neck and spinal surgery. They will instead compete at UFC 334 at New York's Madison Square Garden on Saturday. Nunes beams with excitement at the prospect of returning to the octagon to fight Harrison, and she has lost none of her trademark confidence during her three years away from the sport. "I'm not here today as a challenger, I'm here today as a double champion," said Nunes. "I needed a break and did it at the right time for my mind, body and soul. "There's no hate. It's about the challenge Kayla brings and how great this will be for women's MMA. We want to prove who the best girl is in the cage." top.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
top.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. According to SPORT , Barcelona arranged for a representative to attend the international friendly in Buenos Aires to assess several players, with Martinez among the defenders attracting particular attention. The 28-year-old offers an experienced option for Hansi Flick, whose side continues to explore ways of strengthening their central defence despite the club’s financial restrictions. Notably, Barcelona’s interest is quite significant because Barcelona appear to be considering players who could contribute immediately rather than relying exclusively on younger prospects. top.title: The return of Ronaldinho: PR stunt or genuine comeback?
top.description: Ronaldinho return GFX - Getty/GOAL The 46-year-old retired more than a decade ago, but lower-league Italian side Ravenna insist that he'll return to action this weekend When Ravenna announced the signing of Ronaldinho in June of this year, the common consensus was that it was some sort of publicity stunt. Nobody truly believed that one of the most beloved footballers of all time was making a comeback at 46 years of age. Apparently, the return is real , though. Ronaldinho actually is going to resume his playing career with a third-tier team located on the east coast of Italy that's never even previously played in Serie A. Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani said right from the start of this rather curious tale that the "dream" was for Ronaldinho to make his debut in the derby against local rivals Forli, and it's now set to be realised, with the 2005 Ballon d'Or winner expected to play some part in Sunday's Serie C clash at the Bruno Benelli. So, what on earth is going on? Why is Ronaldinho coming out of retirement? Is it just for one game? Or is he actually making a proper comeback?... 'Jogo bonito' incarnate Ronaldinho is revered as much for his smile as his sensational set of skills When Cipriani bought his hometown club in June 2024, his stated objective was "to make young people of Ravenna fall in love with football". What better way to do that, he thought, than to sign a player that he himself had grown up idolising? "I don't think there’s any other player who inspires such a love for the game as Ronaldinho does," the New York-based businessman told the Gazzetta dello Sport - and it's hard to disagree. One would be hard pressed to find anyone within the footballing community that doesn't like Ronaldinho. He's one of those very rare characters who is universally revered, adored all around the world because he is effectively 'jogo bonito' incarnate, a one-man carnival. There was one very obvious problem with Cipriani's plan, though: Ronaldinho retired in 2018 at 37 years of age, and hasn't played a game of professional football since parting company with Fluminense in 2015. However, the pair had developed "a genuine friendship" after being introduced by Lorenzo Tonetti, the former co-owner of the famous 'Giannino' restaurant that Ronaldinho frequented during his two-and-a-half-year spell with AC Milan between July 2008 and January 2011. Consequently, when Cipriani suggested a return to professional football with Ravenna, the World Cup winner "said yes immediately". "That’s just how things go with Ronnie," Cipriani told Il Resto del Carlino . "If there's a chance to have fun and excite people, he's all in." No mere marketing ploy Ronaldinho hasn't just joined Ravenna as a player - he's also come on board as a shareholder Ronaldinho's lust for life is well-known, and he was visibly touched by the hero's welcome he received when he made his first appearance in Ravenna at a lavish media event in August. top.title: LSU women’s basketball cruises past McNeese, Denver
top.description: After historic blowouts in the first week of the season, the #9 LSU women’s basketball team put up more standard blowouts in the second week of play. Monday, they trounced McNeese 100-43, and Friday, they crushed Denver 101-37. In total, LSU has outscored their opponents 461-137 in their first four games. Monday’s win over McNeese was most notable for the debut of Noa Morro, the 21-year-old freshman out of Spain. She played limited minutes, but she showed off her quick-release three ball and her ability to guard the perimeter. Combined with Anna Minaeva, she forms half of LSU’s post duo that they’ll need in their big games. LSU came out slowly with an 18-10 first quarter, but they found their groove with a 30-point second quarter. The Tigers cruised the rest of the way with solid play and got to 100 with a Mikaylah Williams accidental buzzer-beater three that she intended for after the buzzer. McNeese shot 9/44 from beyond the arc, something LSU had expected coming in. Jada Williams led the team with 12 rebounds, Mikaylah Williams led the scoring with 17 points and assists with eight, and MiLaysia Fulwiley had an absurd stat line of 13 points, seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and four blocks. Friday’s win over Denver saw LSU play more of their big lineup and get Noa Morrow more minutes than she was told she would get. It might also lead to the Tigers practicing their free throws a lot over the next couple days since they finished 19/32 from the line and 3/13 from the stripe in the first half. Other than that, it was a standard LSU blowout victory. The Tigers opened with a 20-12 first quarter before shutting the Pioneers down with a 22-2 second quarter in which they kept them from making a shot for over 12 consecutive minutes across parts of the first and second quarters. LSU ramped up the scoring with 30 in the third and 29 in the fourth, and Mikayla Williams sealed the hundo with a layup. MiLaysia Fulwiley led the team in scoring with 23 points while adding three steals and two blocks. Mikaylah Williams had 20 points, seven rebounds and a career-high six steals. Anna Minaeva led the boards with 10, and Jada Williams led assists with six. LSU is still in the midst of their long homestand next week. On Monday, the Tigers will take on Sun Belt preseason #1 Troy, and on Thursday, they’ll face reigning NEC regular season and tournament champions Fairleigh Dickinson, the latter of which I’ll be covering from the PMAC. Both games will tip at 7:00 p.m. and will be streamed on SECN+. Radio coverage will be on the LSU Sports mobile app or on Talk 107.3 FM in Baton Rouge.

top.title: REBELS: Edmundo - 'The Animal' who erased the line between genius and insanity
top.description: REBELS: Edmundo GFX - GOAL The forward was one of the most naturally gifted players Brazil has ever produced - but also one of its most troubled Sir Alex Ferguson told his Manchester United players before their 2000 Club World Cup clash with Vasco Da Gama that Romario and Edmundo's legs had gone. According to Mark Bosnich, it took them "about 20 seconds to realise that wasn't true". Vasco's famous front two ran rings around United's beleaguered back four - almost quite literally in the case of Edmundo, who, having teed up Romario for the game's opening goal by pouncing on a poor back-pass from Gary Neville, made it 3-0 just before the break with a strike so skilful that even Diego Maradona stated that only a handful of players in football history would have had the "imagination" to even conceive of it, let alone pull off. When Gerson played a short, diagonal pass into Edmundo on the edge of the area, a normal player would have laid the ball off to a team-mate. There was never anything normal about Edmundo, though. The man known as 'The Animal' stabbed the ball with his right foot, thus generating enough spin to flick it behind both himself and Mikael Silvestre, who had made the mistake of getting too close to the attacker. By the time Silvestre realised what Edmundo had done, it was already too late. The Brazilian was gone, taking full advantage of his still-explosive pace to win the footrace with Bosnich to the loose ball, which he subsequently dinked over the goalkeeper with his characteristic nonchalance. Tellingly, Bosnich wasn't even mad; he was impressed, describing it as "the most beautiful goal I've ever conceded", while Silvestre couldn't help but admire the way in which Edmundo had completely bamboozled him. "When you are not used to it, you do not expect such skills," the Frenchman told BBC Sport . "And only geniuses can do what Edmundo did to me for his goal." However, legendary American pianist Oscar Levant once said that he erased "the fine line between genius and insanity" - and, in the case of Edmundo, one could argue that it maybe never even existed in the first place. Beast of a player Edmundo was initially known solely for the quality of his play before his inner rage became a cause for concern There were reports of unusual, erratic or downright bad behaviour from the moment Edmundo began to make a name for himself as a prodigiously gifted teenager in the 1980s. top.title: San Siro - The Scrum
top.description: San Siro - The Scrum How do you get 80,018 people (yes, you read that right, EIGHTY THOUSAND AND EIGHTEEN) into San Siro during the international break? No Inter, no football, but still a ball, albeit an oval one for a change. On 14 November 2009, the All Blacks, New Zealand's legendary national rugby team, arrived at the Meazza to face Italy in a test match that made Italian sporting history. And what better stage than San Siro for an unforgettable Saturday? For the first time, the Meazza opened its doors for a rugby match that went far beyond sport. Italy was taking on New Zealand, the All Blacks, perhaps the most recognisable team in the world, even among those who don't follow rugby. It’s one of the most successful teams, with a remarkable 77% winning record. It was no ordinary Saturday in Milano. The city was filled with the familiar sea of black-clad New Zealand supporters, but above all with rugby fans from across Italy, eager to witness the day Italian rugby dreamed of making history. Kick-off was scheduled for 14:30 CET, making for a packed house not only at the stadium but also in Milano's bars from early in the morning. New Zealand fans had another important fixture to follow: at 8:00 CET, the All Whites, the national football team, were playing Bahrain for a place at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa after a goalless first leg. Mission accomplished, thanks to a header from Rory Fallon, a midfielder then playing for Plymouth in England's second tier. It was New Zealand's first World Cup qualification since 1982, sparking celebrations among supporters back home and in Milano. Just a few months later, New Zealand would face Italy in South Africa and secure a historic draw. It was exactly the kind of miraculous result Italy was hoping to achieve at San Siro. The Meazza erupts as the national anthem rings out, setting the stage for a special afternoon. The crowd can hardly believe its eyes when Italy takes a 3-0 lead through a perfectly struck penalty by Craig Gower. But Luke McAlister's kicks and a try from hooker Corey Flynn put the All Blacks ahead 14-3 at halftime. Everyone expects New Zealand to run riot in the second half. Instead, the All Blacks struggle to break through against an outstanding Italy side that keeps them on edge until the very end. This is the Italy squad which included captain Sergio Parisse, Martin Castrogiovanni and Totò Perugini, Mauro Bergamasco and so many other rugby stars. A team whose strength lies in its formidable scrum, the aspect of the game that perhaps best embodies the spirit of rugby. With eight minutes remaining, Italy pins the All Blacks back in a scrum near the corner between the Curva Sud and the red stand. The Azzurri are more stable, more disciplined, and more united than their opponents. top.title: Real Madrid injury update: Superstar forward expected to return for national team after missing Italy defeat
top.description: Real Madrid injury update: Superstar forward expected to return for national team after missing Italy defeat France and Zinedine Zidane were reminded just how difficult it is to play without Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe. The 27-year-old forward missed Les Bleus ‘ game against Italy with a hamstring injury, and his absence was felt. France lost 3-1 to Roberto Mancini’s side and will be hoping to return to winning ways against Turkey. Now, according to Diario AS , France have received a boost, with Mbappe returning to training ahead of the important game. Mbappe returns to training after injury scare The Real Madrid superstar participated in Friday’s training session at the Matmut Atlantique stadium in Bordeaux. His hamstring discomfort had kept him out of the first game, but his condition has improved considerably, and he now looks ready to return to the pitch. France felt the absence of their captain Kylian Mbappe against Italy. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Zidane had already indicated as much, revealing that the plan had always been to have him available for the game against Turkey. “I hope he is ready for Sunday. That was the plan: for him to rest because he was a little sore and have the chance to play,” Zidane explained. France have always maintained that Mbappe’s absence was strictly precautionary and have insisted that he remain with the squad . Real Madrid hoping to avoid further complications Les Bleus ‘ defeat against Italy has increased the importance of Sunday’s encounter, with Zidane’s side needing a victory over Turkey. France must also hope Italy fail to defeat Belgium if they are to reclaim top spot in their group. A lot is riding on this weekend’s game. Mbappe has been in excellent form under Jose Mourinho. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) For Real Madrid, though, the priority is ensuring France do not rush Mbappe back and that he comes through the game unscathed. Jose Mourinho’s side are extremely dependent on the Frenchman for goals, with Mbappe finding the back of the net in his last seven appearances. While his return to group training is encouraging, Los Blancos would ideally hope that he is not risked against Turkey unless he is 100% fit. With Los Blancos set to face Celta next weekend, Mourinho will hope to have his star striker fully fit for the game. It remains to be seen how things play out.

top.title: Manel Kape Steals Joshua Van’s Flyweight Title After Champion Almost Misses Joint Presser Due to Travel Issues
top.description: The next couple of months promise several scintillating matchups, with UFC 335 set to take place at the T-Mobile Arena on December 12. Meanwhile, UFC 336 will kick off 2027 as the promotion returns to Toronto for its first numbered event in the city on January 30. UFC 335 will feature Charles Oliveira taking on Diego Lopes for the BMF title, while Alex Pereira returns for his second heavyweight outing against Sergei Pavlovich. Meanwhile, UFC 336 will see Joshua Van defend his flyweight championship against Manel Kape, alongside Carlos Prates and Michael Morales battling for interim welterweight gold. To build momentum for both events, the UFC organized a joint kickoff press conference featuring all eight fighters. The event took place at the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where the athletes also participated in face-offs. And it is safe to say that Kape made quite an impression. Already embroiled in a bitter rivalry with Van over the past few months, the Portuguese flyweight took advantage of the champion’s absence during the press conference. With Van’s podium left empty, Kape walked over, picked up the flyweight championship resting on the table, and draped it over his own shoulder. The challenger then proceeded to taunt the absent champion, making it clear that he was already treating the belt as his own. Kape said, “Dana, what the f**k! top.title: Thousands Of Travellers Stranded, 6,000 Flights Canceled, As US Grounds All Airplanes For Hours
top.description: The US grounded all flights for several hours Friday, sparking travel chaos across the vast country, after what government officials said was a major communications outage caused by decades-old technology. The nationwide stop left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events. The incident marked only the second time such an alert had been issued in US airspace since the 9/11 attacks. Federal Aviation Authority officials lifted the groundstop after around four hours, with President Donald Trump’s administration saying there was no evidence the outage was the result of foul play. “This is a legacy system problem,” said Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy. “We have old, old switches, old routers. “We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded.” Duffy on Thursday had formally asked Congress for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System. As the groundstop was lifted, he repeated his plea. “I’m going to say it a million times: the Congress has to give the resources to the president so he can finish this bill,” he said. Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. 6,000 Flights Canceled With almost 6,000 flights canceled, including some international routes according to FlightAware, the recovery from the stoppage was expected to take some time. Footage from airports around the country showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways. Passengers thronged concourses, desperate for information about an outage that had thrown their travel plans into chaos. “We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too,” said Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California. US airspace is among the busiest in the world, and is ramping up to its most frenetic as the Thanksgiving holiday moves into view. A nationwide groundstop is highly unusual; there was one such stop in January 2023 when a pilot notification system failed, but the only other national stop happened in the wake of the 9/11 attacks, when no aircraft took to the skies for days. top.description: Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images Isaiah Stewart and LeBron James were involved in one of the most viral on-court altercations in the history of the NBA. Back in 2021, when the Los Angeles Lakers faced the Detroit Pistons, James caught Stewart in the face while swinging his arm, leaving the latter bleeding. A sophomore at the time, Stewart was furious and involved in a huge altercation with James, which even resulted in a suspension for both players. Now, the former Pistons star has had his say on what happened. Isaiah Stewart says LeBron James hitting him was ‘personal’ For those unaware, in the third quarter of the game between the Lakers and the Pistons, James and Stewart got tangled up while fighting for a rebounding position during a free throw. As he tried to free himself, James’ left arm struck Stewart in the face, causing a cut right above his eye. To his credit, the then-Lakers superstar immediately apologised and even claimed later that the incident was ‘definitely accidental’. ( ESPN ) However, Stewart does not believe James to this day and feels that it was ‘personal’. He said on the Out The Mud Podcast : “Till this day I always say 100%, I know it was personal. You wind up, you hit me. He got a good hit. I’m bleeding. I definitely think it was personal. I’ve seen the interview of him saying it wasn’t. “He gave me a hit, and then I’m like, ‘hold up, hold up.’ And I got up, and then when I saw blood, that’s when I just blacked. I blacked, and I wanted to draw blood back. “Obviously, being a rookie, it’s a lot of stuff going through your mind when that’s happening. What you should do. How you should act. But man, once I saw that blood down my face, I just lost it. “I’m chasing him, trying to get to him around the court. And then I knew I wasn’t getting to him. So I said f*** it. I went to the back, ran to the back, they closed the doors. They said, ‘You got to clean these stitches up.’ I cleaned the stitches up. I got off the table, and I’m still trying to go over to their side. “And then my guy Troy Weaver said, ‘Look, you need to be the person we drafted.’ When he said that, it just clicked. And I said, ‘Let me stop it right here.’” Both players were ejected from the game, and on the following day, the NBA suspended them. James was given a one-game suspension for ‘recklessly hitting Stewart in the face and initiating an on-court altercation’, while Stewart was suspended for two games for ‘escalating an on-court altercation by repeatedly and aggressively pursuing [James] in an unsportsmanlike manner’. A lot has happened since, and the two players are in different stages of their careers – Stewart plays for the Memphis Grizzlies, while James plays for the Philadelphia 76ers. However, when the two sides meet in December, this will surely be the storyline heading into the game. top.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-NOR-PRESSER - AFP Norway captain Martin Odegaard is targeting redemption against Wales on Saturday as the Scandinavian hosts fight to keep their slim Nations League quarter-final hopes alive. Sitting bottom of Group A4, Stale Solbakken's side must win in Oslo to avenge last month's defeat in Cardiff and remain in contention for the last eight. October setback leaves hosts bottom Odegaard is determined to settle the score after goals from Dan James and Neco Williams sealed a 2-1 victory for the Dragons at the Cardiff City Stadium in October . Despite reaching the World Cup quarter-finals this summer, the Scandinavians have suffered three defeats across their current Group A4 campaign. Those three consecutive losses match their total from their previous 23 outings combined, which featured 17 wins and three draws. Skipper demands improved home display Seeking to avoid losing four consecutive matches for the first time since October 2016, the Arsenal playmaker believes his team-mates are ready to bounce back in front of their own supporters . Reflecting on last month's defeat in South Wales, Odegaard said: "Our level was not where it should be. I think it's probably the only game for a long time where we haven't been playing to our standards. "Wales is a good team, a competitive team, lots of good players in big leagues and a physical team as well, and we were prepared for that. "But I think on the day we were just not showing up to our standards, and that's something we want to show [on Saturday], and we can do a lot better. We want to show a different version." Boss anticipates open tactical battle With Craig Bellamy's visitors also requiring three points to preserve their own quarter-final ambitions, head coach Solbakken expects an end-to-end contest: "It's like a boxing [match], going head-to-head, fist-to-fist. "I think Wales has always been a very attacking team under Bellamy. They've had great progress with the ball. "I think it suits the team with the offensive players they have, the speed on the wings and Harry Wilson back. And [Lewis] Koumas getting more minutes for Liverpool, so I think that suits them. nigeria.description: By Steve Oko, Regional Editor, South East The scene at the School of Health Aba, the commercial capital of Abia State last weekend offered a fascinating glimpse into what could become one of the defining political contradictions of the 2027 presidential election. It showed the widening gulf between the political calculations of South East power brokers and the apparent preferences of the ordinary people. It was a moment when political establishment encountered popular sentiment, and the response from the crowd was anything but pretence. The masses, in unmistakable terms, passed a strong message: they are not in for jokes! They know what is good for them. nigeria.description: O’tega Ogra, Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Digital Engagement, Strategy and New Media, has disputed claims that the president’s convoy was attacked by youths following his attendance at Friday prayers at the Shagari Central Mosque in Area 1, Abuja. Tinubu had visited the mosque in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) for the Juma’at prayer on Friday. However, Dino Melaye, a chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), later shared a video showing some youths throwing stones at a convoy believed to belong to the president. In the video, which has circulated widely on social media, some of the youths were heard chanting, “Ba ma yi, ba ma so”, a Hausa expression meaning “we don’t want you; we don’t support you”. nigeria.title: Why 16 Nigerians died transiting through Addis Ababa
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has advised Nigerians, particularly those with underlying health conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the death of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued the advisory on Friday, revealing that Nigeria’s diplomatic mission in Addis Ababa recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the Ethiopian capital. The deaths were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. According to the ministry, Addis Ababa is located about 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen levels. The ministry noted that while most healthy individuals can adapt to such conditions, travellers with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory illnesses may face increased health risks. “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitude,” the statement said. The government therefore urged Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high-altitude environments to seek medical advice before travelling through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are strongly advised to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys,” the ministry stated However, the Federal Government stressed that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. “Rather, it aims to ensure that persons who may be medically vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes are adequately informed and encouraged to take necessary precautions,” the statement added. The ministry reaffirmed the government’s commitment to safeguarding the health, safety and wellbeing of Nigerians abroad through timely travel advisories and other consular support measures. nigeria.title: Egemen Mustafa Şener on the three words he learned in a Black Sea village that still run his business
nigeria.description: Çifteköprü is a small village in the Borçka district of Artvin, in Türkiye’s Eastern Black Sea region. It is the kind of place where the weather decides more of the week than any calendar does, where a neighbour’s word carries the same weight as a document, and where the ground gives back exactly what the work put in. It is also where Egemen Mustafa Şener learned, before he ever ran a construction site in Istanbul or a shipyard project in Montevideo, the three practices that still organise his business today. The three words, as the company itself frames them, are labor, promises, and land. From a Black Sea farm to an Istanbul construction site Şener was born in Çifteköprü in May 1968. His father worked the land, his mother came from a well-established Laz family, and the household ran on a set of unspoken rules that any rural community would recognise. Work was visible or it hadn’t happened. A spoken commitment was binding. The land did not reward shortcuts. When he moved to Istanbul after high school, into business school and then into agricultural trading in the late 1980s, those rules didn’t get left behind. By the early 1990s, when he had shifted into residential and commercial construction and was managing his first sites in the city, the same three practices were doing the actual work of running the business. The language of the construction industry was new, but the habits underneath it were the same ones he had grown up with. Egemen Mustafa Şener on labor, in a sector where everything has to be seen The first of the three is labor, and in construction it is not a metaphor. Every person on a site contributes something that is either visible in the finished work or hidden inside it. A good site manager is one who can see the work that is supposed to be hidden as clearly as the work on the surface. Visible labor is also what makes delivery possible. A project is a stack of promises about what will happen on which date, and every one of those promises rests on someone actually doing the work. When labor becomes abstract, delivery slips. In three decades of residential, commercial, industrial and infrastructure projects, this has not changed. The promise that does the work before the contract does The second word is promises. In most business settings, promises are secondary to contracts. In the one Egemen Mustafa Şener grew up in, they were the contract. A spoken commitment was held because the alternative, in a village the size of Çifteköprü, was impossible to live with. Transplanted into construction, that habit becomes a working style. A contract will specify the delivery date and the quality standard. But between any two reasonable parties, the real agreement is the one that was given before the paperwork caught up, and the business that honours that version tends to finish projects on terms that match what was actually said. nigeria.title: Lumumba identifies what’s fueling xenophobia
nigeria.description: •Says Africa cannot fight poverty by turning against fellow Africans Professor Patrick Loch Otieno (PLO) Lumumba has warned that Africa’s failure to create sufficient economic opportunities is fuelling xenophobia. He urged governments to address unemployment, poverty and weak industrial development rather than blame migrants for the continent’s challenges. Lumumba, a renowned Kenyan legal scholar and public speaker, said xenophobia often thrived in societies experiencing economic hardship, where unemployment, inequality and pressure on public services encouraged citizens to regard foreigners as competitors. He spoke as the keynote speaker at the Bridge Club’s grand end-of-year event in Lagos on Thursday. In his address, titled Africa Must Not Become Foreign to Itself: Xenophobia, Pan-Africanism and the Future of African Belonging, Lumumba argued that migrants were frequently made scapegoats for economic problems arising from poor governance and weak institutions. He said: “The foreign trader, worker or entrepreneur can be arrested. The failure to create productive employment over several decades cannot be arrested at a roadblock.” According to him, African governments must look beyond the presence of migrants and examine the structural weaknesses responsible for unemployment, poverty and economic competition. He said the inability of many African countries to industrialise and create productive jobs had forced millions of young people into informal economic activities, where competition for limited opportunities could generate resentment. Lumumba observed that Africa’s economic dependence on exporting raw materials while importing finished products had contributed to the loss of employment opportunities to other economies. “We export crude oil and import refined petroleum. We export cocoa and import chocolate. We export minerals and import the machines, batteries and technologies manufactured from them,” he said. He added that the continent was effectively creating employment opportunities elsewhere while its young population continued to struggle for limited opportunities at home. The legal scholar said the appropriate response to the exploitation of migrant workers was to enforce labour laws against employers rather than encourage hostility towards foreigners. According to him, employers who engage undocumented migrants and pay them below lawful wages create resentment among local workers while benefiting from the division. “The appropriate response is not violence against the migrant. Lumumba also highlighted the contradiction in Africans celebrating the achievements of their compatriots abroad while treating migrants from other African countries with hostility. nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC) took a decisive turn when Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, invalidated the emergence of Senator David Mark and other executives who assumed control of the party in July 2025. But the judgment of November 5, 2026, was not simply about competing claims to party leadership. It hinged on a fundamental legal question: could the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC) use its constitutional powers to replace an existing elected leadership structure without complying with the democratic procedures prescribed by law? In the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment obtained by Saturday Vanguard, Justice Lifu said he identified critical weaknesses in the defendants’ case, including the disputed resignation letter on which they relied, the limits of NEC’s administrative powers and the absence of satisfactory evidence that the new executives emerged through a democratic election. The resignation letter One of the Mark-led camp’s principal arguments was that Nafiu Bala Gombe had voluntarily resigned as Deputy National Chairman on May 17, 2025, before the NEC meeting that produced the new leadership. The letter, tendered as Exhibit ADC 1, was intended to establish that Gombe had relinquished his position and consequently lacked the legal standing to challenge the subsequent leadership transition. Justice Lifu, however, was unconvinced Rather than accept the document simply because it was certified, the judge examined its signature against Gombe’s signatures on other documents executed before a Commissioner for Oaths. He explained that certification established the status of a document as a true copy but did not, in itself, establish the authenticity of a disputed signature. After comparing the documents, he said that he found material differences in their structure, style, formation and general manner of execution. “The signatures do not appear to be one and the same,” Justice Lifu observed. He consequently described the purported resignation letter as fictitious or fabricated and rejected it as reliable evidence that Gombe had voluntarily vacated his office. The finding removed a central pillar of the defendants’ argument that Gombe had ceased to be an officer of the party before the July 2025 transition. Importantly, this was a finding made in determining the civil dispute, not a criminal conviction for forgery. nigeria.description: The United States has reopened its airspace after a nationwide ground stop triggered by a communications failure at air traffic control centres disrupted thousands of flights and left tens of thousands of passengers stranded at airports across the country. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted the restriction on Friday, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announcing that US airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (0115 GMT on Saturday). However, Duffy warned that flight operations would resume gradually, adding that airlines would need time to restore normal schedules. “It’s going to be slow,” he told reporters at the White House. According to flight-tracking platform FlightRadar24, more than 6,600 flights were cancelled and 8,600 delayed, while another 1,500 flights had already been cancelled for Sunday. Aviation analysts warned that the four-hour nationwide grounding could disrupt airline operations for several days. Duffy said tens of thousands of passengers were stranded at airports nationwide following the disruption. He disclosed that he and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had met with President Donald Trump at the Oval Office to discuss the incident. What caused the disruption Duffy said the problem began at 3:36 p.m. when air traffic control centres experienced instability in their radar and communications systems. According to him, switches and routers became overloaded with data, resulting in inconsistencies in information transmitted through the network and prompting authorities to shut down the affected system. “Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data and they started to give us inconsistencies in the data from those routers and because of that we shut the system down,” he said. He maintained that authorities never completely lost radar or communications capabilities and were able to land thousands of aircraft safely. Duffy said the immediate technical problem had been resolved and that flying was safe, but stressed the need for a comprehensive upgrade of the country’s ageing air traffic control infrastructure. FG seeks $50bn for aviation overhaul The Transportation Secretary blamed inadequate congressional funding for delays in modernising the country’s air traffic control system, calling for $50 billion to overhaul the infrastructure. Earlier on Friday, before the disruption, the White House and the Department of Transportation had urged Congress to approve $30.1 billion for upgrades to the nation’s ageing airports and air traffic control infrastructure. “What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system,” Duffy said. “Give us the money to fix it.” Meanwhile, Mullin said there was no evidence so far that the incident resulted from a cyberattack or a rogue artificial intelligence system, although investigators had not ruled out either possibility. “It appears this was mechanically driven, however, we’re still looking,” he said. entertainment.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. An alumna of Yale University (where she earned her B.A.) and Yale Law School (where she earned her J.D.), Emehelu is a proud resident of Montclair, New Jersey, where she and her husband, Ike , raised their two children, Nnamdi and Amara . entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. About FWIFT Nigeria The Forum For Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. entertainment.title: Toni Tones and Jim Iyke Are Bringing Drama to KAVA This November — See the Official Poster
entertainment.description: The Nigerian thriller series, directed by Wande Thomas and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi, is set to join KAVA’s growing slate of premium African content. Nigerian streaming platform KAVA is set to bring the psychological thriller series Spiraling , starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys ) and Jim Iyke , to audiences across its streaming service. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives. Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms , Seun Ajayi , Fae Olumide , Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba . Created and directed by Wande Thomas ( Under the Influence , The Smart Money Woman ), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi ( The Smart Money Woman , Ci ) . Director and creator Wande Thomas added: I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. Ladun Awobokun , Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented : Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. entertainment.title: From Talking Drums to Tourism Diplomacy: How Nigeria Captured Attention at WTM London 2026
entertainment.description: With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities. For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London. Led by the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA), under its Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, the Nigeria Pavilion welcomed international visitors, tourism professionals, Nigerians and Africans living in the United Kingdom, and industry stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria. Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery. Together with the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA) and diaspora media partners, Nigeria created an experience that extended beyond destination marketing. Day One: Nigeria Arrives in Colour and Rhythm The opening day brought the Nigeria Pavilion to life with traditional talking drums, cultural performances, networking and opportunities for visitors to experience Nigeria’s creative identity. From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country. Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity. The Director General Who Stole the Show Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance. Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase. sports.title: The challenge that brought Nunes out of retirement
sports.description: Amanda Nunes is one of four simultaneous two-division champions in UFC history [Getty Images] It was always going to take a special challenge to bring Amanda Nunes out of retirement. The Brazilian left the UFC in 2023 as the most successful women's mixed martial artist of all time, and with a strong claim to be the greatest ever, regardless of gender. A former featherweight and bantamweight champion, Nunes is the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts. During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko. After Nunes was eventually dethroned by Julianna Pena in one of the biggest upsets of all time, she then regained her title in emphatic fashion. Nunes was so dominant, she ran out of challengers and left the sport feeling like she had completed MMA. That was until Kayla Harrison came along. "When Kayla signed with the UFC and I saw the division with some new girls it excited me," said Nunes. "Because I cleaned both divisions and didn't have anything to do any more. That was when I was sure I wanted to do this again." American Harrison is a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo who became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion after transitioning to MMA. After joining the UFC in 2024, Harrison won the bantamweight title in only her third fight with the promotion. The contest between 36-year-old Harrison and 38-year-old Nunes is being described by pundits as one of the biggest women's fights in UFC history. The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, before Nunes left in 2022. They were originally set to fight in January, but the fight got postponed after Harrison required neck and spinal surgery. They will instead compete at UFC 334 at New York's Madison Square Garden on Saturday. Nunes beams with excitement at the prospect of returning to the octagon to fight Harrison, and she has lost none of her trademark confidence during her three years away from the sport. "I'm not here today as a challenger, I'm here today as a double champion," said Nunes. "I needed a break and did it at the right time for my mind, body and soul. "There's no hate. sports.description: Ronaldinho return GFX - Getty/GOAL The 46-year-old retired more than a decade ago, but lower-league Italian side Ravenna insist that he'll return to action this weekend When Ravenna announced the signing of Ronaldinho in June of this year, the common consensus was that it was some sort of publicity stunt. Nobody truly believed that one of the most beloved footballers of all time was making a comeback at 46 years of age. Apparently, the return is real , though. Ronaldinho actually is going to resume his playing career with a third-tier team located on the east coast of Italy that's never even previously played in Serie A. Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani said right from the start of this rather curious tale that the "dream" was for Ronaldinho to make his debut in the derby against local rivals Forli, and it's now set to be realised, with the 2005 Ballon d'Or winner expected to play some part in Sunday's Serie C clash at the Bruno Benelli. So, what on earth is going on? Why is Ronaldinho coming out of retirement? Is it just for one game? Or is he actually making a proper comeback?... 'Jogo bonito' incarnate Ronaldinho is revered as much for his smile as his sensational set of skills When Cipriani bought his hometown club in June 2024, his stated objective was "to make young people of Ravenna fall in love with football". What better way to do that, he thought, than to sign a player that he himself had grown up idolising? "I don't think there’s any other player who inspires such a love for the game as Ronaldinho does," the New York-based businessman told the Gazzetta dello Sport - and it's hard to disagree. One would be hard pressed to find anyone within the footballing community that doesn't like Ronaldinho. He's one of those very rare characters who is universally revered, adored all around the world because he is effectively 'jogo bonito' incarnate, a one-man carnival. There was one very obvious problem with Cipriani's plan, though: Ronaldinho retired in 2018 at 37 years of age, and hasn't played a game of professional football since parting company with Fluminense in 2015. However, the pair had developed "a genuine friendship" after being introduced by Lorenzo Tonetti, the former co-owner of the famous 'Giannino' restaurant that Ronaldinho frequented during his two-and-a-half-year spell with AC Milan between July 2008 and January 2011. Consequently, when Cipriani suggested a return to professional football with Ravenna, the World Cup winner "said yes immediately". "That’s just how things go with Ronnie," Cipriani told Il Resto del Carlino . "If there's a chance to have fun and excite people, he's all in." sports.description: After historic blowouts in the first week of the season, the #9 LSU women’s basketball team put up more standard blowouts in the second week of play. Monday, they trounced McNeese 100-43, and Friday, they crushed Denver 101-37. In total, LSU has outscored their opponents 461-137 in their first four games. Monday’s win over McNeese was most notable for the debut of Noa Morro, the 21-year-old freshman out of Spain. She played limited minutes, but she showed off her quick-release three ball and her ability to guard the perimeter. Combined with Anna Minaeva, she forms half of LSU’s post duo that they’ll need in their big games. LSU came out slowly with an 18-10 first quarter, but they found their groove with a 30-point second quarter. The Tigers cruised the rest of the way with solid play and got to 100 with a Mikaylah Williams accidental buzzer-beater three that she intended for after the buzzer. McNeese shot 9/44 from beyond the arc, something LSU had expected coming in. Jada Williams led the team with 12 rebounds, Mikaylah Williams led the scoring with 17 points and assists with eight, and MiLaysia Fulwiley had an absurd stat line of 13 points, seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and four blocks. Friday’s win over Denver saw LSU play more of their big lineup and get Noa Morrow more minutes than she was told she would get. It might also lead to the Tigers practicing their free throws a lot over the next couple days since they finished 19/32 from the line and 3/13 from the stripe in the first half. Other than that, it was a standard LSU blowout victory. The Tigers opened with a 20-12 first quarter before shutting the Pioneers down with a 22-2 second quarter in which they kept them from making a shot for over 12 consecutive minutes across parts of the first and second quarters. LSU ramped up the scoring with 30 in the third and 29 in the fourth, and Mikayla Williams sealed the hundo with a layup. MiLaysia Fulwiley led the team in scoring with 23 points while adding three steals and two blocks. Mikaylah Williams had 20 points, seven rebounds and a career-high six steals. Anna Minaeva led the boards with 10, and Jada Williams led assists with six. LSU is still in the midst of their long homestand next week. On Monday, the Tigers will take on Sun Belt preseason #1 Troy, and on Thursday, they’ll face reigning NEC regular season and tournament champions Fairleigh Dickinson, the latter of which I’ll be covering from the PMAC. Both games will tip at 7:00 p.m. and will be streamed on SECN+. Radio coverage will be on the LSU Sports mobile app or on Talk 107.3 FM in Baton Rouge.

sports.title: REBELS: Edmundo - 'The Animal' who erased the line between genius and insanity
sports.description: REBELS: Edmundo GFX - GOAL The forward was one of the most naturally gifted players Brazil has ever produced - but also one of its most troubled Sir Alex Ferguson told his Manchester United players before their 2000 Club World Cup clash with Vasco Da Gama that Romario and Edmundo's legs had gone. According to Mark Bosnich, it took them "about 20 seconds to realise that wasn't true". Vasco's famous front two ran rings around United's beleaguered back four - almost quite literally in the case of Edmundo, who, having teed up Romario for the game's opening goal by pouncing on a poor back-pass from Gary Neville, made it 3-0 just before the break with a strike so skilful that even Diego Maradona stated that only a handful of players in football history would have had the "imagination" to even conceive of it, let alone pull off. When Gerson played a short, diagonal pass into Edmundo on the edge of the area, a normal player would have laid the ball off to a team-mate. There was never anything normal about Edmundo, though. The man known as 'The Animal' stabbed the ball with his right foot, thus generating enough spin to flick it behind both himself and Mikael Silvestre, who had made the mistake of getting too close to the attacker. By the time Silvestre realised what Edmundo had done, it was already too late. The Brazilian was gone, taking full advantage of his still-explosive pace to win the footrace with Bosnich to the loose ball, which he subsequently dinked over the goalkeeper with his characteristic nonchalance. Tellingly, Bosnich wasn't even mad; he was impressed, describing it as "the most beautiful goal I've ever conceded", while Silvestre couldn't help but admire the way in which Edmundo had completely bamboozled him. "When you are not used to it, you do not expect such skills," the Frenchman told BBC Sport . "And only geniuses can do what Edmundo did to me for his goal." However, legendary American pianist Oscar Levant once said that he erased "the fine line between genius and insanity" - and, in the case of Edmundo, one could argue that it maybe never even existed in the first place. Beast of a player Edmundo was initially known solely for the quality of his play before his inner rage became a cause for concern There were reports of unusual, erratic or downright bad behaviour from the moment Edmundo began to make a name for himself as a prodigiously gifted teenager in the 1980s. sports.title: San Siro - The Scrum
sports.description: San Siro - The Scrum How do you get 80,018 people (yes, you read that right, EIGHTY THOUSAND AND EIGHTEEN) into San Siro during the international break? No Inter, no football, but still a ball, albeit an oval one for a change. On 14 November 2009, the All Blacks, New Zealand's legendary national rugby team, arrived at the Meazza to face Italy in a test match that made Italian sporting history. And what better stage than San Siro for an unforgettable Saturday? For the first time, the Meazza opened its doors for a rugby match that went far beyond sport. Italy was taking on New Zealand, the All Blacks, perhaps the most recognisable team in the world, even among those who don't follow rugby. It’s one of the most successful teams, with a remarkable 77% winning record. It was no ordinary Saturday in Milano. The city was filled with the familiar sea of black-clad New Zealand supporters, but above all with rugby fans from across Italy, eager to witness the day Italian rugby dreamed of making history. Kick-off was scheduled for 14:30 CET, making for a packed house not only at the stadium but also in Milano's bars from early in the morning. New Zealand fans had another important fixture to follow: at 8:00 CET, the All Whites, the national football team, were playing Bahrain for a place at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa after a goalless first leg. Mission accomplished, thanks to a header from Rory Fallon, a midfielder then playing for Plymouth in England's second tier. It was New Zealand's first World Cup qualification since 1982, sparking celebrations among supporters back home and in Milano. Just a few months later, New Zealand would face Italy in South Africa and secure a historic draw. It was exactly the kind of miraculous result Italy was hoping to achieve at San Siro. The Meazza erupts as the national anthem rings out, setting the stage for a special afternoon. The crowd can hardly believe its eyes when Italy takes a 3-0 lead through a perfectly struck penalty by Craig Gower. But Luke McAlister's kicks and a try from hooker Corey Flynn put the All Blacks ahead 14-3 at halftime. Everyone expects New Zealand to run riot in the second half. Instead, the All Blacks struggle to break through against an outstanding Italy side that keeps them on edge until the very end. This is the Italy squad which included captain Sergio Parisse, Martin Castrogiovanni and Totò Perugini, Mauro Bergamasco and so many other rugby stars. A team whose strength lies in its formidable scrum, the aspect of the game that perhaps best embodies the spirit of rugby. With eight minutes remaining, Italy pins the All Blacks back in a scrum near the corner between the Curva Sud and the red stand. The Azzurri are more stable, more disciplined, and more united than their opponents.
